examples.question_text: Two similar solids have matching lengths in the ratio $4:7$. Find the ratio of their surface areas and the ratio of their volumes.
examples.solution_text:
Square each term for surface areas.
$\begin{align*}\text{Surface area ratio}&=4^2:7^2\\&=16:49\end{align*}$
Cube each term for volumes.
$\begin{align*}\text{Volume ratio}&=4^3:7^3\\&=64:343\end{align*}$

examples.question_text:
a. Two similar figures have areas in the ratio $36:49$. Find the ratio of their matching lengths.
b. Two similar solids have volumes in the ratio $125:216$. Find the ratio of their matching lengths.
examples.solution_text:
a. Take the square root of each term.
$\begin{align*}\text{Length ratio}&=\sqrt{36}:\sqrt{49}\\&=6:7\end{align*}$
b. Take the cube root of each term.
$\begin{align*}\text{Length ratio}&=\sqrt[3]{125}:\sqrt[3]{216}\\&=5:6\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A triangle with area $32\text{ cm}^2$ is enlarged by scale factor $k=1.5$. Find the area of the enlarged triangle.
examples.solution_text:
Length ratio, original : image, is $1:1.5$.
$\begin{align*}\text{Area ratio}&=1^2:1.5^2\\&=1:2.25\end{align*}$
The ratio table is
$\begin{array}{c|cc}&\text{Original}&\text{Image}\\\hline\text{Area ratio}&1&2.25\\\text{Area }(\text{cm}^2)&32&72\end{array}$
$\begin{align*}A_2&=32\times2.25\\&=72\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A similar copy of a solid is made using scale factor $k=\frac12$. The original volume is $96\text{ cm}^3$. Find the volume of the copy.
examples.solution_text:
Length ratio, original : copy, is $1:\frac12$.
$\begin{align*}\text{Volume ratio}&=1^3:\left(\frac12\right)^3\\&=1:\frac18\end{align*}$
The ratio table is
$\begin{array}{c|cc}&\text{Original}&\text{Copy}\\\hline\text{Volume ratio}&1&\frac18\\\text{Volume }(\text{cm}^3)&96&12\end{array}$
$\begin{align*}V_2&=96\times\frac18\\&=12\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$

Square the ratio of matching lengths.
$\begin{align*}\frac{A}{18}&=\left(\frac96\right)^2\\\frac{A}{18}&=\frac94\\A&=18\times\frac94\\A&=40.5\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: Two similar jars have heights $15\text{ cm}$ and $25\text{ cm}$. The larger jar holds $2.5\text{ L}$. Find the capacity of the smaller jar.
examples.solution_text:
Cube the ratio of matching heights.
$\begin{align*}\frac{V}{2.5}&=\left(\frac{15}{25}\right)^3\\\frac{V}{2.5}&=\frac{27}{125}\\V&=2.5\times\frac{27}{125}\\V&=0.54\text{ L}\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: Two similar solids have volumes in the ratio $64:125$. Find the ratio of their heights and the ratio of their surface areas.
examples.solution_text:
Take cube roots to find the length ratio.
$\begin{align*}\text{Height ratio}&=\sqrt[3]{64}:\sqrt[3]{125}\\&=4:5\end{align*}$
Square the length ratio to find the surface area ratio.
$\begin{align*}\text{Surface area ratio}&=4^2:5^2\\&=16:25\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: Two similar solids have surface areas in the ratio $16:49$. Find the ratio of their volumes.
examples.solution_text:
Take square roots to find the length ratio.
$\begin{align*}\text{Length ratio}&=\sqrt{16}:\sqrt{49}\\&=4:7\end{align*}$
Cube the length ratio to find the volume ratio.
$\begin{align*}\text{Volume ratio}&=4^3:7^3\\&=64:343\end{align*}$

examples.question_text:
A map uses a scale of $1:2000$.
a. A garden covers $1.2\text{ cm}^2$ on the map. Find its actual area in $\text{m}^2$.
b. A playing field has actual area $800\text{ m}^2$. Find its area on the map in $\text{cm}^2$.
examples.solution_text:
The area ratio, map : actual, is $1:2000^2=1:4\,000\,000$.
a.
$\begin{align*}A_{\text{actual}}&=1.2\times4\,000\,000\\&=4\,800\,000\text{ cm}^2\\&=480\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$
b. Convert the actual area to square centimetres, then divide by the area factor.
$\begin{align*}A_{\text{actual}}&=800\times100^2\\&=8\,000\,000\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{map}}&=8\,000\,000\div4\,000\,000\\&=2\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$

examples.question_text:
a. A box holds exactly $180$ identical marbles. A similar box has every dimension three times as large. Assuming the same packing, how many marbles will it hold?
b. A solid metal ball is melted and recast into similar balls, each with $\frac16$ of the original radius. Assuming no metal is lost, how many smaller balls can be made?
examples.solution_text:
a. The capacity scales by the cube of the length factor.
$\begin{align*}N&=180\times3^3\\&=180\times27\\&=4860\text{ marbles}\end{align*}$
b. Each smaller ball has $\left(\frac16\right)^3=\frac1{216}$ of the original volume.
$\begin{align*}N&=1\div\frac1{216}\\&=216\text{ balls}\end{align*}$

examples.question_text:
A dog is modelled as a similar animal with every length increased by a factor of $5$.
a. By what factor does its volume increase?
b. By what factor does the surface area of its tongue increase?
c. If heat production scales with volume and cooling by the tongue scales with its surface area, explain why cooling becomes more difficult.
examples.solution_text:
a. Volume factor $=5^3=125$.
b. Tongue surface area factor $=5^2=25$.
c. Heat production increases by a factor of $125$, while the tongue's cooling area increases by only $25$. There is five times as much heat production per unit of cooling area.

coverage.summary: Authored 11 worked examples covering all distinct assessed methods, with one mapping for each of the 34 exact assessment locators. Used changed values and the supplied booklet's ratio, ratio-table and proportional-equation methods. Questions and solutions remain separate; solution prose inherits renderer blue. Aligned working uses relation-sign gutters without unnecessary phantom equals. examples.derivation: Squaring 4:7 gives surface areas 16:49; cubing gives volumes 64:343. This also covers deriving both quantities from one length ratio.
Square roots of 36 and 49 give 6:7. Cube roots of 125 and 216 give 5:6.
The area factor is 1.5 squared, or 2.25. Multiplying 32 by 2.25 gives 72 cm²; both ratio-table rows agree.
The volume factor is (1/2) cubed, or 1/8. Multiplying 96 by 1/8 gives 12 cm³; the ratio table agrees.

The matching-length factor is 9/6 = 3/2, so the area factor is 9/4. The larger area is 18 × 9/4 = 40.5 cm². Diagram dimensions scale uniformly by 1.5, labels match the givens, and no answer is exposed.
The smaller-to-larger height ratio is 15/25 = 3/5. Its cube is 27/125, giving capacity 2.5 × 27/125 = 0.54 L.
Cube roots convert volume ratio 64:125 to height ratio 4:5. Squaring gives surface area ratio 16:25.
Square roots convert surface area ratio 16:49 to length ratio 4:7. Cubing gives volume ratio 64:343, using the source's combined ratio rules.
The area factor is 2000² = 4,000,000. Part a gives 4,800,000 cm² ÷ 10,000 = 480 m². Part b gives 800 × 10,000 = 8,000,000 cm², then division by 4,000,000 gives 2 cm².
Under the stated packing assumption, 180 × 3³ = 4860 marbles. Each recast ball uses (1/6)³ = 1/216 of the original volume, giving 216 balls with no metal lost.
Volume increases by 5³ = 125 and tongue area by 5² = 25. Under the stated model, heat production per unit cooling area increases by 125/25 = 5.
